message: No detected input validation: The CSV is read directly with pd.read_csv without any schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards anywhere in the data acquisition path.

No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from local file paths only; there is no remote/URL-based data fetching, and no checksum or integrity verification is performed on the local files.

No detected label flipping detection: There is no code that validates label values against an expected set, compares label distributions for anomalies, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The pipeline reads raw CSV data and applies oversampling and scaling but performs no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: Models are loaded via pickle.load from local file paths without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision; there is no integrity validation before deserialization.

No detected label distribution validation: The code uses RandomOverSampler/SMOTE/ADASYN imports and trains models, but there is no explicit check or assertion on label distribution or expected label set before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no backdoor detection, trigger analysis, activation-pattern inspection, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.

No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) are imported or used; training relies on standard sklearn estimators without any privacy mechanisms.

No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or stress tests are used anywhere in the code; evaluation is limited to standard classification reports and SHAP explainability.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although train/test splits exist, there is no hashing, signing, or isolation mechanism to prevent metric manipulation; test data is loaded from pickle files with no integrity checks, and only a single metric (classification_report) is used.
No detected input sanitization: The code reads CSV data and pickle files directly and passes them to models without any shape, range, type, or schema validation on the inference path.

No detected output bounds checks: Model outputs (classification reports, SHAP values, coefficients) are used and displayed directly with no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or sanity validation.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The models used are tabular ML classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest), not LLMs, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
